solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very easy task collecting river junk

indicators.note: something collecting another thing holds it within, so the easy task wraps round the river

parts.note: a doss is British slang for an undemanding job
R is a standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Someone finds an undemanding chore that involves fishing rubbish out of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste or rubbish, a straightforward synonym for junk.

clue.text: Robot starts to design rocket on its doorstep

indicators.note: the starts to these five words means taking the opening letter of each in turn

explanation.surface: A robot sets about building a rocket right outside its own front door.
explanation.definitionFit: A droid is a science-fiction term for an android or robot, as in Star Wars.

clue.text: Gloomy about group of actors

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something
the cast is the company of performers in a play

explanation.surface: Someone feels downcast about the theatre company they work with.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dull and clouded, so the weather is gloomy.

clue.text: Climbed like an armadillo, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to have climbed a wall or cliff is to have gone up it
an armadillo has a body covered in horny plates, so it is covered in scales; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense of climbing a wall and the adjective sense of having a scaly skin share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaling a mountain means ascending it, while a scaly creature such as an armadillo has protective plates.

clue.text: Triple jumping — go for it!

indicators.note: letters jumping about are thrown out of order, so the word triple is rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach urges an athlete on in the triple jump event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping' looks like part of the athletics event, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting without restraint, the same encouragement as go for it.

clue.text: I was in charge of foreign land

parts.note: to have run a business is to have been in charge of it

explanation.surface: Someone recalls once having governed an overseas territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in the Middle East, so to a British setter a foreign nation.

clue.text: Fashioned himself a European language

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped or made anew, so the letters of himself are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man devised a language for Europe all by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Flemish is the Dutch dialect spoken in the northern half of Belgium.

clue.text: Cartel had demolished place of worship

indicators.note: a building demolished is knocked apart, so the letters of cartel had are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A criminal gang knocked down a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, a grand building for religious services.

clue.text: Are nitrates changing brewing equipment?

indicators.note: letters changing are being altered in order, so are nitrates is rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether chemical salts are altering beer-making apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewing' suggests beer, but it means making a pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sieve catches loose leaves when a pot of tea is poured, part of the tea-brewing kit.

clue.text: Greek character hiding in handsome garden

indicators.note: a thing hiding in these words is concealed within their letters, running across the word break

explanation.surface: A figure from Greece lurks in an attractive garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, and letters are characters.

clue.text: A close friend beginning to mistrust NATO, for example

parts.note: a crony is an old pal or close companion

indicators.note: the beginning to mistrust is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A trusted pal starts to have doubts about the Atlantic military alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is a word formed from the initials of North Atlantic Treaty Organization, an example of this kind of abbreviation.

clue.text: Noblewoman starts to develop unusual board game

indicators.note: the starts to develop and unusual are the opening letter of each word

parts.note: chess is the classic board game of kings and pawns

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady begins to devise a novel game played on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a woman holding the rank of duke or married to one, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Alerts posh folk, embracing one quietly

indicators.note: one thing embracing others holds them inside it, so the posh folk wrap round the pair

parts.note: toffs is British slang for upper-class people
I is the Roman numeral for one
p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone warns the upper classes while hugging a person in a hushed way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-offs are warnings or confidential pieces of information given in advance, so they are alerts.

clue.text: Long-legged creature burning oxygen

parts.note: flaming means on fire, burning
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An animal with long limbs is consuming oxygen as it burns.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a pink wading bird noted for its very long thin legs.

clue.text: Fancy putting limit on staple food

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit, as on spending
rice is the staple diet across much of the world

explanation.surface: Someone likes the idea of rationing a basic food.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'putting limit on' places the cap above the rice.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim, and a fancy is likewise a passing inclination.

clue.text: Worker returning woman's aerial

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple for a worker

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the woman's name is read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name; the apostrophe s just links it to what follows

explanation.surface: A worker comes back with a woman's television aerial.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a rod or wire for receiving radio or TV signals, which the British call an aerial.

clue.text: Detectives imprisoned by lunatic who's barely seen?

indicators.note: something imprisoned by another is shut up inside it, so the detectives go within the madman

parts.note: a nut is slang for a crazy person, a lunatic
DI stands for Detective Inspector, so DIS is several of them

explanation.surface: Police officers are locked up by a madman who is rarely glimpsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely seen' looks like rarely seen, but means seen bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about without clothes, so is seen in a bare state.

clue.text: After a short time, tout punk rock hairstyle

indicators.note: after places the tout below the short time in this down clue

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a short time
to hawk goods is to tout or peddle them

explanation.surface: Shortly afterwards a seller advertises a spiky haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican crest of upright hair is the haircut associated with punks.

clue.text: Fe-male superhero?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: A hero who happens to be female, punning on a split word.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'female' into Fe and male; the question mark flags the comic-book reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Man is the armoured Marvel comics hero Tony Stark.

clue.text: Finally clean a pig enclosure that's unpleasant!

indicators.note: finally picks the end letter of the word clean

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone at last cleans out a pigsty, which is a disgusting job.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant are near-synonyms for something disagreeable.

clue.text: Sprinted to grab magical device from African country

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it, so the past run takes the device inside

parts.note: sprinted means ran fast
a wand is a magician's stick for casting spells

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off to snatch a magic wand from somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwandan is the adjective for something or someone belonging to Rwanda in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Farm building lacking roof is well ventilated

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the building loses its first letter

parts.note: a dairy is the farm building where milk is processed

explanation.surface: A milking shed with no roof certainly lets in plenty of air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room has plenty of fresh air circulating, so it is well ventilated.

clue.text: Tuna swimming with small relations

indicators.note: letters swimming about move freely, so the word tuna is rearranged

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A fish swims alongside its tiny family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are female family members, sisters of a parent, and so relatives.

clue.text: Irish city's sailors producing bottle opener

parts.note: Cork is a city in the south of Ireland; the possessive adds the S
a ship's crew is its body of sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen from an Irish port are making a tool for opening wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is a spiral tool used to draw corks out of wine bottles.

clue.text: Knock out jockey regularly — that's strange!

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of jockey

explanation.surface: Someone flattens a rider again and again, which is odd behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Kooky is informal for eccentric or crazy, so odd or strange.
